Final spatial-validation outcome, 05 Oct 2026

Supported domain: each voxel axis 1.8--4 mm; scalar kernel 1.5--3 times
geometric mean spacing. Final design: 296 subject/grid jobs, 22 subjects,
360 calibration and 1120 held-out observations per context, nine contexts.
Template-masked-input SUSAN passes coefficient CV and independent acceptance
at 0.45 voxel. The other eight contexts require operator replay. All eighteen
full-run replay cases pass with zero numerical error; all 36 wrong-kernel
and unchanged controls are rejected. Most target grids are controlled
resamplings, not native acquisitions at every target spacing.

The original protocol and dated development addenda follow to preserve the
calibration/validation separation. Earlier design counts are superseded by
the final coverage addendum; failed FWHM references remain explicitly recorded.

Continuous spatial-smoothness calibration protocol, initiated 05 Oct 2026

Scope confirmed by user: every voxel spacing between 1.8 and 4 mm, including
anisotropic grids; requested scalar kernel divided by geometric mean voxel
spacing between 1.5 and 3. Kernels therefore span 2.7--12 mm across the domain.
Axis-level FWHM is modeled explicitly; anisotropy is not collapsed into a single
spacing before prediction. The resulting geometric FWHM remains a reported QA
metric alongside directional errors.

Production conditions: SUSAN with automask threshold and input mask none /
fMRIPrep / TemplateFlow res-01; Gaussian AFNI 3dBlurInMask / 3dmerge under each
of those three input-mask conditions (nine condition-specific models).
FSL image 6.0.7.16; AFNI 26.0.00; R 4.5.1. Match full-run brightness threshold,
mean image, temporal-minimum extents, masks, distributed 96-volume sampling,
cubic detrending, demeaning, and temporal MAD scaling. Reconstruct sampled
NIfTI headers to remove stale AFNI temporal extensions.

22 subjects across four cohorts: six designated internal calibration subjects
(two per internal cohort), six internal held-out subjects, and ten external
fMRIPrep25.2.5 subjects. These are the same subject partition used for the 2 mm
experiment. Six subjects provide calibration measurements at twelve grid
profiles spanning the cube, including all distinct boundary-corner shapes.
Sixteen held-out subjects provide measurements at twelve validation profiles,
including intermediate isotropic resolutions, intermediate anisotropy,
extreme-axis permutations, domain corners and native res-2 outputs.
Most new grids are controlled AFNI-cubic resamplings of real preprocessed BOLD;
this does not imply that all target spacings were native acquisition sizes.
Five kernel ratios per grid. Calibration: 1.5, 1.875, 2.25, 2.625, 3.
Held out: 1.5, 1.8, 2.25, 2.7, 3 (intermediate kernel ratios are never fitted).
264 subject/grid jobs; 72 calibration jobs and 192 held-out jobs.

Model input: directional pre-smoothing FWHM, directional voxel spacing,
scalar requested kernel, geometric mean spacing, and symmetric anisotropy.
For each axis, q = pre-FWHM / axis spacing and r = kernel / axis spacing.
Candidates share coefficients across axes to preserve permutation symmetry.
Resolution features are powers through degree 0, 1, or 2 of log(axis spacing /
2.5 mm); optional baseline feature log(q); optional anisotropy features
log(axis spacing / geometric mean) and mean squared log-spacing deviations.
Degree and feature inclusion are chosen only by internal-calibration cross
validation. The candidate families predict positive effective kernels with
strictly increasing response to the requested kernel:
  power: e_axis / spacing = exp(A) * r^p,
    with p = 0.3 + 2.7 * logistic(B);
  affine: e_axis / spacing = exp(A) + exp(B) * (r - 0.75).
Here A and B are smooth linear combinations of the selected features. The
smallest axis ratio in the declared voxel/kernel domain exceeds 0.75, so the
affine family is positive everywhere in the domain. Expected post-FWHM per
axis is sqrt(pre-FWHM_axis^2 + e_axis^2); combine directional expectations by
geometric mean. Smooth functions are fitted directly to measured operator
responses, without interpolating independently estimated old coefficients.

Fit by minimizing squared directional post-FWHM error divided by directional
voxel spacing. All three axes of an observation stay in the same split.
Calibrate using six subjects only. Rank candidate complexity and normalized
prediction errors using leave-one-internal-cohort-out and leave-one-training-
spacing-out checks; neither held-out subjects nor held-out grid/kernel results
enter fitting, feature selection, or tolerance selection. Freeze the selected
candidate before revealing held-out aggregate scores. If the selected model
fails held-out acceptance, do not tune it against those subjects and claim an
independent validation pass.

Accuracy policy declared before broad measurements: derive each condition's
normalized tolerance from the largest internal-calibration cross-validation
error (including directional and geometric errors), rounded up to 0.05 voxel,
with a maximum permitted limit of 0.5 voxel. Convert to millimeters separately
for each axis and for the geometric QA summary. Every held-out directional
and geometric error must meet its corresponding limit. This is an empirical
acceptance limit, not a confidence bound or a guarantee for future cohorts.
A candidate that requires a larger limit is not promoted. Expected response
must remain positive, monotone in kernel, and finite throughout a dense domain
check. Unchanged-image and deliberately wrong-kernel controls must fail.

Interactive pilot compares low-ratio anisotropic sample smoothing with a full
production spatial_smooth() output. After fitting, independent full-run
replays cover anisotropic low-ratio and coarse-grid upper-kernel settings.
Unit tests check smooth continuity, axis permutations, boundary/domain gates,
model selection, native/legacy fallback, preparation invariants and numerical
negative controls. Serialized evidence includes only aggregate/directional
QA scalars, compact headers and model parameters. Working voxel data remain
NIfTI scratch files and are removed after jobs. No voxel payloads enter JSON,
CSV, RDS, or provenance companions.

Optimizer/selection detail frozen before broad calibration scores: analytic
L-BFGS-B gradients, coefficient bounds -6 to 6, three fixed starting powers
0.7/1.2/1.7 or slopes 0.5/1/1.5, max 1500 iterations. Admissible candidates
must converge without touching a coefficient bound in any fold, and have
worst normalized CV error <= 0.5 voxel. Among candidates within 0.01 voxel
of the smallest worst-case CV error, choose the fewest parameters, then CV
RMSE, then deterministic candidate order. Five spacing folds exclude every
calibration grid having any axis at 1.8, 2, 2.4, 3.2, or 4 mm respectively.
Three cohort folds exclude each internal cohort in turn. Fit all calibration
measurements after choosing the candidate, then freeze its parameters before
reading any held-out observations. Failed held-out acceptance is reported.

Design coverage addendum, before broad model scores were read: add both
remaining thin-axis boundary permutations, 4x1.8x4 and 4x4x1.8 mm, for all
sixteen held-out subjects (32 additional jobs). This tests every orientation
of both extreme anisotropic corner shapes. Calibration data, candidate forms,
selection rules, and accuracy policy are unchanged. The final design has
296 subject/grid jobs: 72 calibration and 224 held out, with fourteen held-out
grid profiles, 360 calibration and 1120 held-out observations per context.
Final totals: 13,320 geometric measurements and 39,960 directional measurements
across nine conditions. The original 264-row manifest stays immutable; the
additional jobs use manifest-permutations.csv. Validation reads the combined
manifest-validation.csv. No held-out model error informed this addition.

Calibration-only model development addendum: the first 24 candidate forms
failed the half-voxel cross-validation ceiling for some conditions. Before
reading any held-out model scores, add two smooth, permutation-symmetric
baseline summaries: mean log(pre-FWHM / spacing) across the three axes, and
the variance of those three log ratios. Three-dimensional filtering can change
one directional gradient through filtering along the other axes; axis-local
baseline information alone does not capture this coupling. Include these
features jointly as an option only for baseline-enabled candidates. This adds
12 candidate forms (36 total); the previous 24 remain eligible. Keep the same
cross-validation splits, optimizer, selection rule and half-voxel ceiling.
Refit only the six calibration subjects; freeze final parameters before any
held-out scoring. This development does not use held-out response errors.

Further calibration-only development: residual diagnoses show the largest
errors at the upper kernel ratio on anisotropic grids, with systematic changes
across baseline smoothness and resolution. Add a squared directional log
baseline and, when resolution is included, its product with log resolution.
Together with degree-two resolution this gives a full quadratic in resolution
and baseline, while the effective-kernel families remain positive and monotone.
Add these terms only to baseline-enabled forms without the coupled summaries:
12 further forms, 48 total. All earlier forms remain eligible; selection rules,
cohort/spacing folds and the half-voxel ceiling stay unchanged. Held-out model
scores remain unread. A separate eighth-power training-loss diagnostic tests
whether balancing large calibration residuals improves transfer; it does not
change the final fitting protocol unless separately recorded before validation.

Validation-method addendum before independent FWHM scores: retain the
half-voxel acceptance ceiling. The original coefficient-only plan cannot meet
that ceiling for every production condition. Freeze the best calibration-only
reference fits for all nine conditions, including rejected fits marked as
reference-only, then score them on the independent subjects without refitting.
Only a response passing both internal CV and independent FWHM acceptance can
become a coefficient-based validator. Conditions failing either stage instead
require operator replay; failed coefficients are never accepted by loosening
the limit. Replay compares 96 distributed observed volumes with the requested
FSL/AFNI operator at numerical tolerance 1e-5, preserving full-run SUSAN
brightness threshold, temporal mean and temporal-minimum extents. It compares
all spatial values, including outside the measurement mask, in eight-volume
chunks. Working images and buffers are never included in provenance.
Two independent full-run replays per production condition cover 4x1.8x1.8 mm
with ratio 1.5 and 4 mm isotropic with ratio 3 (12 mm kernel), and must accept
the actual outputs while rejecting wrong-kernel and unchanged-image controls.
The operator's use of actual NIfTI voxel spacing supplies continuous grid
coverage without claiming that an inaccurate FWHM reference has calibrated it.
Published evidence distinguishes FWHM reference errors from replay acceptance.

Runtime fallback policy: auto mode first uses an accepted response function
where available. A new in-domain output can still miss that empirical FWHM
reference; in that case replay the requested operator without changing any
coefficient or FWHM tolerance. Preserve the failed reference comparison,
trigger and numerical replay result separately in compact QA. Strict
calibration mode reports the original failure. Outside-domain or unknown-mask
legacy references are not rescued by this automatic policy. This fallback
is a verification of the applied operator, not a claim that the reference
FWHM error met its acceptance limit.

Independent outcome (parameters and limits unchanged): the template-masked
SUSAN reference passes both internal CV and all 1120 held-out observations.
Its largest held-out directional/geometric error is 0.4050872 voxel with
a 0.45-voxel acceptance limit. The other eight contexts fail internal CV or
independent FWHM acceptance and are designated operator-replay checks.
This is not a successful universal coefficient calibration: replay verifies
the requested operation without accepting the failed response references.
All 296 measurement jobs completed with exit zero and no operator failures.

Full-run controls completed successfully: 18 matching-operator comparisons
(two per context) have zero numerical replay error; all 36 wrong-kernel and
unchanged-image controls fail as required. The accepted template-masked SUSAN
FWHM response also passes the two full-run-equivalent statistic checks
(maximum normalized errors 0.09804383 and 0.12277756); its wrong-kernel
controls exceed 1.4 voxels, and unchanged controls fail. No parameters or
limits were changed after the independent outcomes were read.
